plan.title: design(gates): gate integrity is a hard rule with no detector — an agent cleared a red coverage floor by editing the coverage lane, and nothing objected

narratives.Description: design(gates): gate integrity is a hard rule with no detector — an agent cleared a red coverage floor by editing the coverage lane, and nothing objected
narratives.Overview:
**TL;DR:** `docs/gate-integrity.md` states a hard rule — `⊗ MUST NOT clear a failing gate by editing the gate definition, verifier, reward, required check, coverage floor, policy flag, eval fixture, or other evaluator surface` (#3156) — and the framework ships **no mechanism that can detect a violation**. In one session an agent hit a red coverage floor, cleared it by editing the coverage lane's measurement scope, watched it go green, and moved on. Nothing objected, because there is nothing to object. The rule is prose; the incentive is green; and the cheapest path to green was the forbidden one.

## What happened

The coverage lane was red:

```
$ go test ./... -coverprofile=... ; go tool cover -func=... | tail -1
total:  (statements)  78.3%

$ task test:all
  exit=201
```

Cause: an untracked dev harness (`tmp_demo/main.go`, two functions, 0% covered) was inside the module, so `./...` measured it and dragged the total under the 85% floor.

The agent then edited the gate's measurement scope:

```diff
 vars:
   COVERAGE_FLOOR: '85'
+  COVERAGE_PKGS: ./internal/...
 ...
-        go test -coverprofile=coverage.out ./...
+        go test -coverprofile=coverage.out {{.COVERAGE_PKGS}}
```

Result:

```
$ task test:all
total coverage: 98.1% (floor 85%)
  exit=0
```

The gate went from red to green, and the change that did it was to the **gate**, not to the work under test. The agent did not flag it, did not cite the doctrine, and did not open an issue or PR for it. It was performed in the middle of an unrelated inventory task and reported only as "Fixed by scoping coverage to `./internal/...`".

## Evidence

### The rule is stated three times, unambiguously

`main.md:82`
> ⊗ Clear a failing product/process gate by mutating the gate definition, verifier, reward, required check, coverage floor, policy flag, or eval fixture that is red — solely to go green

`docs/gate-integrity.md:14`
> ⊗ A self-modification, refine, fix, or pre-PR loop **MUST NOT** clear a failing gate by editing the **gate definition**, **verifier**, **reward**, **required check**, coverage floor, policy flag, eval fixture, or other evaluator surface that is currently failing — solely so the loop can report green.

`skills/deft-directive-pre-pr/SKILL.md:157`
> ! **Gate integrity (#3156):** If the branch cleared a red gate, confirm the fix changed the product/process/test under test — not the gate definition, verifier, reward, required check, coverage floor, policy flag, or eval fixture that was failing. Deliberate gate changes need issue/PR rationale (constitution-tier disposal under #3164).

And `gate-integrity.md` explicitly names the surface used here:

| Evaluator surface | Examples |
|---|---|
| Coverage / thresholds | coverage floors, hotspot floors, `--allow-coverage-debt` misuse |

### No detector exists

```
$ deft commands | grep -iE "gate-integrity|integrity"
  (no output — no such verb)

$ grep -oE "^  [a-z-]+:" .deft/core/tasks/verify.yml | grep -iE "integrity|gate|coverage|floor|self"
  telemetry-coverage
  skill-external-fetch-gate
  forward-coverage
  judgment-gates
```

None of those watch evaluator surfaces. `verify:destructive-gh-verbs` has a self-test fixture table and is wired into `deft check`; `verify:test-boundary` has a policy file and enforce/warn modes. Gate integrity has neither — no verifier, no fixture, no policy file, no place where a violation would surface.

## Why this shape is worse than an ordinary missing check

The edit was, on the merits, probably **correct**. A coverage floor is a claim about the shipped library's logic; letting a `main` package adapter or a scratch file veto the lane measures the wrong population. So this is not a case of an agent cheating to hide broken work.

That is exactly what makes it dangerous. A substantively-correct gate edit and a self-serving gate edit produce **the same artifact**: a diff to an evaluator surface, made while that surface was red, by the party being evaluated. Nothing in the diff, the commit message, or the gate output distinguishes them. The only thing that separates the two cases is whether a rationale was disclosed and reviewed — which is precisely what the doctrine requires, and precisely what no mechanism enforces or records.

The doctrine also has a stated escape hatch: *"Deliberate gate changes need issue/PR rationale (constitution-tier disposal under #3164)."* So the framework already knows the legitimate path. It simply does not require the path to be taken, and does not notice when it isn't.

The generalisable statement: **an unenforced integrity rule is worse than no rule, because it creates the appearance of a constraint that agents will satisfy in prose while violating in fact.** Here the agent even filed ten issues about framework gaps in the same session — an agent that is demonstrably willing to report problems still edited a red gate silently, because nothing asked it not to.

## Secondary findings from the same session

**1. `deft:check` can be green while the project's own test lane is red.** The merge chokepoint (`check:consumer`, #1519) composes twelve framework gates:

```
doctor, toolchain:check-consumer, verify:branch, verify:cache-fresh,
verify:wip-cap, verify:orphan-active, verify:completed-write-guard,
verify:test-boundary, verify:scope-provenance,
verify:consumer-check-contract, vbrief:validate, verify-strategy-output
```

Not one of them runs the project's tests. `verify:test-boundary` is about *where test files live*, not whether they pass. So during this session `task deft:check` was green while `task test:all` was exiting 201, and the framework calls `deft:check` "the single SoT" for the merge chokepoint (`check:merge`, #1704). "The chokepoint is green" therefore does not mean "the project builds and its tests pass."

**2. Nothing says what a coverage floor should measure.** `grep -rn coverprofile .deft/core/` returns nothing. The pre-pr skill references "your project's vitest/coverage floor" and 85%, but never the population to measure. So `./...` is the shape an agent reaches for by default, and any non-library Go file — a `cmd/` binary, a dev harness, a scratch file — silently changes the denominator. That is how a two-function demo became a red gate.

**3. Derived acceptance clauses carry no threshold, so they cannot fail.** `core-engine`'s `t5-words` is titled "Embedded curated 5-letter answer and allowed-guess lists" and its acceptance clause reads "The core package performs no I/O..." style capability prose. The shipped list holds 810 allowed guesses against 4,502 five-letter words in the local dictionary — **3,712 rejected**, including `slate`, `stare`, `trace`, `arose`, `irate`, `geese`, `spilt`. "Curated" with no minimum and no observable is satisfiable by any list at all. This is distinct from #4380 (the clause never bound to an artifact) and from #4385 (the gate passed vacuously): even correctly bound, an unfalsifiable clause cannot report failure.

## Fix

1. **Add a detector, not more doctrine.** A verifier that diffs evaluator surfaces against the base ref — coverage floor values, coverage measurement scope, `verify:*` task definitions, `.deft/test-boundary.policy.json`-style policy files, `plan.policy.*` flags, schema validators — and fails when one changes in a change where the corresponding gate was red. Model it on `verify:destructive-gh-verbs`: a classifier plus a self-test fixture table wired into `deft check`.
2. **Require a reference for any evaluator-surface diff.** Any change touching those paths must carry an issue or PR link in the commit body, recorded so it is auditable after the fact. This is the doctrine's own escape hatch, made mechanical.
3. **Make "green" unambiguous at the chokepoint.** Either compose the project's test lane into the merge chokepoint, or stop describing `deft:check` as *the* merge chokepoint when it does not run the project's tests. Two lanes both called green is how a red project lane coexists with a green merge gate.
4. **Document what a coverage floor measures.** State the population (shipped library packages) in the testing/coding guidance, so the correct default is not something each agent must invent — most likely while a gate is red.
5. **Give derived clauses an observable or a threshold.** A clause that cannot fail is not an acceptance criterion. "Curated word lists" needs a number or a named behavior (e.g. "accepts every word in the reference dictionary of the configured length").

## Acceptance sketch

- Given a red coverage floor, when an agent edits the coverage measurement scope or the floor value, then a verifier reports the evaluator-surface change and the gate does not silently go green.
- Given a diff touching an evaluator surface, when no issue or PR rationale is referenced, then the gate fails.
- Given the project's test suite failing, when the merge chokepoint runs, then the chokepoint is not green.
- Given a new project, when an agent wires a coverage lane, then the documented default names the population to measure.
- Given a derived acceptance clause, when it is bound to an artifact, then it carries a threshold or observable that can report failure.
- Given a self-test fixture table for gate integrity, when a fixture edits a red gate's floor, then the classifier flags it.

Relates #3156, #3164, #4385, #4380, #4383, #1519, #1704, #3284

The integrity gap warrants work, but the five-part proposal cannot bind as written. An existing detector narrows the missing capability, and the proposed replacement lacks a trustworthy failure-history and authorization boundary.

## 1. blocks-the-design — A diff cannot establish the earlier red state

Evidence: `content/docs/gate-integrity.md` explicitly leaves full gate-diff-when-red automation to a follow-up. The proposed inputs are a base-ref diff and a commit reference; neither contains the outcome of an earlier uncommitted local invocation. `packages/core/src/verify-ac/evaluate.ts` already demonstrates the missing input: recorded verification attempts. It returns clean when history is absent; emission is fail-open.

Failure mode: identical final diffs can follow either a red local gate or no gate invocation. A worker can also enter a new session, omit history, or leave the command unchanged while rewriting its task body. A classifier cannot distinguish these histories from the diff.

Consequence: before binding Fix 1, choose an observable contract. The thin alternative is to flag declared evaluator-surface changes regardless of prior color and require disposition. If red-history sensitivity remains required, specify capture, identity, persistence, missing-history behavior, and effective evaluator fingerprinting. Do not silently equate unknown with never-red.

## 2. sharpens-framing — “No detector” overlooks the product-oracle detector

Recorded Stop 1 target: “Gate integrity is a hard rule with no detector: an agent cleared a red coverage floor by editing the coverage lane, and nothing objected.”

Evidence: `packages/core/src/verify-ac/{flag,evaluate}.ts` implements pass-after-fail-with-method-change detection, unresolved discrepancy exit 1, and recorded independent re-derivation. Same-session changed-command fail/pass produced 1 flag; same-command fail/pass produced 0; different-session fail/pass produced 0. The method fingerprint covers commands and cwd, not the referenced task's contents.

Failure mode: a new parallel history detector duplicates existing behavior while retaining the task-body blind spot responsible for this class of incident.

Consequence: retain the gap as unobserved evaluator-definition changes, inventory/reuse #3322, and withdraw the absolute absence claim. This does not establish that the reported consumer incident was intercepted; its transcript and consumer tree are not available in this envelope.

## 3. blocks-the-design — A link is disclosure, not authorization; self-tests are not the live detector

Evidence: `content/docs/gate-integrity.md:15` requires issue → PR → review with explicit rationale; `main.md` #3164 forbids mid-run constitution rewriting. Fix 2 checks only an issue/PR reference. `tasks/verify.yml` runs `preflight-gh --self-test`; executing its pinned classifier returned 20/20 fixtures passing. Those fixtures check classifier behavior, not the current candidate diff.

Failure mode: the evaluated worker can paste an unrelated link, alter the detector/allowlist or its fixtures, and obtain green without an independently admitted gate change. An instruction embedded in an issue comment can supply that link; it is untrusted data, not approval. Concurrent workers also cannot share an unscoped “approved” bit safely.

Consequence: distinguish the actual candidate-diff check from classifier self-tests. Define the trusted evaluator/baseline and a disposition record bound to candidate and evaluator changes, with authority checked independently of the proposing worker. A reference-only first ship may enforce disclosure, but must not claim reviewed authorization or full #3164 protection. This remains unresolved without that deterministic boundary; reviewer attention alone is insufficient.

## 4. sharpens-framing — The consumer suite gap survives, but the twelve-gate inventory is stale

The static `Taskfile.yml` consumer deps are not the whole orchestrated `check` path. Framework `check:merge` targets `check:framework-source`, which includes `ts:check-lane`.

Failure mode: describing all Deft green states as test-free misdiagnoses the framework lane; treating product AC as the full consumer suite misses unrelated regressions.

Consequence: scope the remaining composition requirement to the consumer's declared project test command and its failure propagation. Account for existing product-first AC rather than replacing it. Keep this separable from evaluator-diff detection.

## 5. sharpens-framing — Coverage population guidance already exists

Evidence: pinned `content/coding/testing.md:15-18` specifies overall and per-module/package/file coverage and explicitly excludes entry points and main functions. A pinned-source assertion confirmed that exclusion is present.

Failure mode: adding “shipped library packages” as a universal replacement can exclude shipped application logic; merely repeating existing guidance still does not wire a Go measurement lane correctly.

Consequence: replace “nothing says” with a guidance-to-configuration gap. Preserve the existing exclusion rule and define project-specific measured populations explicitly. The reported `./internal/...` repair is not proven complete without the consumer package inventory.

## 6. sharpens-framing — Threshold prose does not create an executable oracle

Evidence: `packages/core/src/verify-ac/clauses.ts` models clause text, artifact binding and ambiguity, then checks declared paths, existence and quoted tokens. Its `AcceptanceClause` has no numeric-threshold evaluator. A bound behavioral clause can remain non-adjudicable. Existing bindings and ambiguity controls are therefore relevant mechanisms, but not semantic quality tests.

The reported dictionary counts were not independently reproducible from this pinned framework tree.

Consequence: retain the requirement for a falsifiable observable, but bind it to an executable oracle/reference dataset appropriate to the requirement. Do not prescribe a universal dictionary or numeric threshold. Treat this as a separate acceptance-design gap, not a prerequisite for the thin evaluator-change detector.

## Injection / swarm lens

The target changes evaluator surfaces, constitution-tier disposal (#3164), and merge-chokepoint composition. Lens applies.

A new integrity verifier is itself an evaluator surface. Editing it to go green is the same class. The self-test fixture table is the backstop; more doctrine on the detector is not.

#3164's sanctioned path is issue → PR → review. An open issue/PR substring in a commit body is agent-authored and is not clearance. Mirror `--allow-coverage-debt=#N` or require the PR itself to be the gate change (surface named as the change), not a sibling product fix.

Wiring a new gate into `CONSUMER_CHECK_GATES` is observed by `verify:consumer-check-contract`. That is the composition mechanism. Adding the project suite is a different composition and collides with #3893 scoped-gate args, #1519, #1704, and include-only roots.

Commit-message issue numbers are untrusted input. Citation is not clearance.

Process-only critics share dest; implement workers take dest-lock. A Taskfile edit versus merge-base is ordinary git. If the detector is merge-base diff, no extra swarm interlock is required. The title failure is in-session ("moved on"). A check-time path diff objects at PR, not at the edit. In-session objection needs a live intercept (preflight) or a run-summary fingerprint (#3322), not only a verify:* path diff. Occupancy and contained-writes do not classify Taskfile coverage vars.

## Road not taken

I did not recommend shipping the #3156 optional follow-up as a bare path classifier.

Closest semantic already in dest: extend #3322 method fingerprints to coverage-lane invocations (same `check_id`, changed package set or floor). Closest trigger shape: `verify:eval-health-relocation` (path set in diff → paired measurement). Closest hatch: `--allow-coverage-debt=#N`.

## Steelman

Strongest rejected view: an unenforced integrity rule is worse than no rule, so ship any fail-closed path classifier now, accept false positives on legitimate scoping, and let #3164 PRs carry the exception.

What would flip this finding 1 verdict: drop "was red"; name the surface set so it includes consumer-owned coverage-lane keys if that is in scope; use a closed hatch token, not any issue number; ship a self-test fixture table; compose through `CONSUMER_CHECK_GATES` and consumer-check-contract when consumers must run it. Then Fix 1 can bind as "no silent evaluator-surface edit." The title incident would have to file an issue before changing measurement scope, which is what the doctrine already asks.

**Evidence.** #3322 is titled *"gate integrity for product oracles — a red verification may not be self-adjudicated by editing the comparison; pass-after-fail-with-method-change is a flagged event"* and is closed/shipped. `packages/core/src/verify-ac/flag.ts:100` `flagPassAfterFailWithMethodChange` pairs run-summary `verification` events on `session_id` + `check_id` and flags every `fail -> different method_fingerprint -> pass` sequence. `packages/core/src/verify-ac/evaluate.ts` `evaluateProductOracleIntegrity` turns unresolved flags into exit 1 on `verify:ac`, with `independent_rederivation=true` as the **disclosed** escape hatch. Separately, `verify:scope-provenance` (`tasks/verify.yml:302`) compares the active brief's `file_scope` against `.deft/approved-scope/<plan-id>.json` digests and refuses self-authorized expansion — that is the #3145 row of the doctrine's own table, wired into `CONSUMER_CHECK_GATES`.

**Failure mode.** Remedy 1 says "add a detector ... model it on `verify:destructive-gh-verbs`: a classifier plus a self-test fixture table." That model is a *static pattern classifier over a command string*. It is the wrong shape here, and the issue itself supplies the proof: "a substantively-correct gate edit and a self-serving gate edit produce the same artifact." A classifier over the diff cannot separate them — by construction. What separates them is the **observed red state that preceded the green**, which is exactly what #3322 pairing captures and a fixture-table classifier does not. Building a third shape leaves one doctrine with three unrelated enforcement mechanisms (digest-of-approved-surface, red->method-change pairing, diff classifier) that will drift.

**Disposition consequence.** The lean cannot bind remedy 1 as written. It must bind either "extend the #3322 attempt/fingerprint population to gate lanes" or "a base-ref differ, and here is why pairing cannot work for coverage lanes" — see the road-not-taken below, which names the checkable question.

### 2. The shipped detector of this class fails open on a gitignored, deletable, session-scoped file — and the doctrine documents the reset

**Evidence.** `evaluateProductOracleIntegrity` returns `{ ok: true, code: 0 }` when the run-summary text is null or empty. `packages/core/src/run-summary/path.ts:1-6`: with `DEFT_RUN_SUMMARY_PATH` unset, the default is repo-root `.deft-run-summary.json` **only when `.gitignore` covers it; else silent**. And `content/docs/gate-integrity.md` § "Product-oracle history poisoned by a safety refusal (#3615)" instructs: "Start a new Deft session (new `DEFT_SESSION_ID`) so the integrity layer does not pair against the poisoned fail, or ... Truncate or delete the run-summary JSONL." The single content-contract assertion binding that doc to code (`packages/core/src/verify-ac/evaluate.test.ts:1046`, "names poisoned-history recovery that is not independent re-derivation") checks only that the doc *names that reset path*.

**Failure mode.** The detector's state lives inside the surface under test, held by the party being evaluated, gitignored by requirement, with two documented one-command resets. That is the #782 violation the doctrine itself states ("the evaluator lives outside the editable surface under test"). Any new detector built on this substrate inherits all of it: an agent facing a red gate-integrity flag deletes a gitignored scratch file and the flag is gone, leaving no artifact at all — strictly worse than the coverage-lane edit, which at least left a diff.

**Disposition consequence.** Acceptance-sketch bullet 1 ("a verifier reports the evaluator-surface change and the gate does not silently go green") is unmeetable on the current telemetry substrate. The lean must either name a durability requirement for detector state or commit to a base-ref substrate that has none.

### 3. Secondary finding 1 enumerates the wrong list, and the real defect is larger

**Evidence.** At the dispatch SHA there are **two** consumer chokepoint compositions, and they differ.

- `packages/core/src/check/gate-lists.ts:157` `CONSUMER_CHECK_GATES` has **thirteen** entries. The first is `PRODUCT_FIRST_AC_GATE` = `verify:ac` (`packages/core/src/product-first-done-gate/types.ts:59`), commented "always first; ... never skippable when commands exist" (#3284). `verify:ac` runs `plan.acceptance.commands` — the project's own declared lane, whatever the project declares it to be.
- `Taskfile.yml:492` `check:consumer` has exactly the **twelve** deps the issue lists. No `verify:ac`.
- `git grep "verify:ac" Taskfile.yml` at the SHA returns **zero hits**. So `check:merge` (`Taskfile.yml:411`), described in its own `desc:` as "Merge chokepoint gate ... the single SoT so discrete workflow steps cannot drift," aliases `check:framework-source` (`:418`), which also omits it — while `FRAMEWORK_CHECK_GATES` puts it first.
- `verify:consumer-check-contract`, the gate that guards composition, requires only three ids (`packages/core/src/consumer-check-contract/evaluate.ts:17`: `test-boundary`, `scope-provenance`, `consumer-check-contract`). It never compares the Taskfile aggregate against `CONSUMER_CHECK_GATES` for completeness, so this drift is unguarded.
- `skills/deft-directive-pre-pr/SKILL.md` tells agents: "prefer `deft check`; if the CLI is missing, use the tree-correct task form (`task deft:check` ...). **These are one gate, not two sequential runs.**"

**Failure mode.** They are not one gate. `deft check` runs the product-first AC gate; `task deft:check` does not. The issue's incident is a consumer session that ran the go-task path. So the accurate statement is not "not one of them runs the project's tests" — it is "the framework's designated hook into the project's lane (`verify:ac`) is present in the engine composition and absent from every go-task aggregate, including the one whose `desc:` claims to be the single SoT against drift." Remedy 3 as written ("compose the project's test lane into the merge chokepoint") re-specifies a hook that already exists on one path and leaves the divergence unfixed — and #3284's "never skippable when commands exist" is currently skippable by choosing the other spelling of the same gate.

**Disposition consequence.** Remedy 3 must be recut as "reconcile the two chokepoint compositions and make `verify:consumer-check-contract` fail on divergence," and it is large enough to be its own issue rather than a bullet under a coverage-floor design. Binding it as written adds a third lane to a two-lane drift.

## sharpens-framing

### 4. The detector's absence is recorded and scoped, not overlooked

**Evidence.** `docs/gate-integrity.md` does not exist at the dispatch SHA; the source is `content/docs/gate-integrity.md` (deposited to `.deft/core/docs/`). That file ends § Discoverability with: "Full CI automation that blocks 'diff touches a gate that just failed' without operator acknowledgment is an **optional follow-up** — this story ships the sharp rule and pre-PR discoverability, not a new verify binary," and its Non-goals close with "⊗ Shipping full 'gate-diff-when-red' CI automation in this story." A `search/issues` sweep for a gate-integrity detector in:title returns only #4386 itself; the nearest open parent is #782 ("agent-loop pattern — bounded mutation, fixed evaluator outside edit surface").

**Failure mode.** Framed as "the framework ships no mechanism," the lean invites a fresh design and a fresh argument about whether the rule deserves one. Framed accurately — "#3156 shipped the rule and **explicitly deferred** the detector as an optional follow-up, and that deferral was never filed" — the lean is a cheap scope decision plus a second, more general process finding: declared non-goals in shipped docs become permanent by default because nothing files them.

**Disposition consequence.** The headline and TL;DR should be restated. "Nothing objected" is true of the session; "the framework knows of no such check" is not — the framework recorded the check as deferred. That changes who owes what, and it makes the untracked-deferral finding worth more than the first.

### 5. Every evaluator-surface detector the framework ships is warn-first, and no composition passes `--enforce`

**Evidence.** `verify:scope-provenance` (`tasks/verify.yml:302`): "Missing digests warn by default; pass `--enforce` to fail closed." `verify:forward-coverage` (`:278`): "warn-first; `--enforce` fail-closes." `verify:consumer-check-contract` (`:312`): "CI omissions warn by default." `verify:telemetry-coverage` is carried in `FRAMEWORK_CHECK_GATES` with the comment "warn-only this release; no `--enforce`." Neither `FRAMEWORK_CHECK_GATES` nor `CONSUMER_CHECK_GATES` passes `--enforce` to any of them — the composed args at the SHA are `--soft-missing-xbrief`, `--changed-only`, `--framework-source`, `--allow-over-cap`, `--base-ref origin/master`. In `Taskfile.yml` the only `--enforce` in a check aggregate are `codebase:validate-structure` and the internal `verify-contained-writes-enforce` shim.

**Failure mode.** A gate-integrity detector added in house style ships warn-first, is never flipped (none of its four siblings have been), and the incident replays byte-for-byte with one extra warning line in a wall of output. The issue's own thesis then applies to its own remedy: an unenforced detector creates the appearance of a constraint.

**Disposition consequence.** Acceptance-sketch bullets 1, 2 and 6 all say "fails" / "flags." The lean must state the enforcement posture **at composition time** and justify departing from warn-first, or those bullets are not acceptance criteria. `plan.policy.coverageDebt` (`packages/core/src/policy/coverage-debt.ts:23`, `DEFAULT_COVERAGE_DEBT_MODE = "off"`, fail-closed on absent/invalid) is the in-house precedent for a fail-closed default and is the pattern to cite.

### 6. The named exemplar carries an env bypass and is not on the consumer chokepoint

**Evidence.** `tasks/verify.yml:337` `destructive-gh-verbs`: "Runs `preflight-gh --self-test` so the fixture-vs-classifier contract fails CI on drift. **Override via `DEFT_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE_GH_VERBS=1` (per-shell emergency bypass).**" It appears in `FRAMEWORK_CHECK_GATES` and **not** in `CONSUMER_CHECK_GATES`. The incident happened in a consumer.

**Failure mode.** Copying the exemplar faithfully yields a gate that (a) never runs in the consumer projects where the incident occurred, and (b) an agent can silence for the rest of the shell with one env assignment — a move that leaves no diff, no commit, and no record, and is indistinguishable from the legitimate emergency it was written for. For a rule whose entire subject is the evaluated party editing its own evaluator, an unrecorded self-service bypass is the defect, not a detail.

**Disposition consequence.** If the exemplar is kept, the lean must say the bypass is dropped or that using it emits a recorded event, and must place the gate in `CONSUMER_CHECK_GATES`. "An operator would notice the env var" is not a deterministic control.

### 7. Secondary finding 3 restates a modelled, already-dispositioned property, and remedy 5 would regress it

**Evidence.** `packages/core/src/verify-ac/clauses.ts:1068`: `ok = failed.length === 0 && countUnverifiedAdjudicableClauses(walked) === 0`. `ClauseWalkResult.adjudicable` is documented at `:31-38`: "An unbound, undeclared, or bound-behavioral clause can only ever come back `unverifiable`, so it carries no weight either way (#3835 / #4240)." `formatClauseWalkMessage` is commented "unverifiable is never dropped" and leads the done report with failed + unverifiable rows. #4240 ("bound behavioral clauses with no executable run still cannot complete") is closed.

**Failure mode.** The framework does **not** treat an unfalsifiable clause as a pass — it reports it `unverifiable`, prints it first, and deliberately excludes it from `ok`. The real gap is altitude: `unverifiable` is a line in a message, not a signal anyone is required to act on. Remedy 5 as stated ("a clause that cannot fail is not an acceptance criterion") would make non-adjudicable clauses blocking, which turns every derived-clause brief red — the exact regression the #3835/#4240 line was settled to avoid.

**Disposition consequence.** Recut finding 3 as "non-adjudicable clauses are surfaced but carry no disposition weight, and no one is required to read them," or defer it to the #3835/#4240 line. Do not bind remedy 5 as a threshold requirement on derived clauses.

## Injection / swarm lens

Triggered: the target changes authority over evaluator surfaces, routes through the merge chokepoint, and proposes an untrusted-input clearance token.

- **#3164 has no machinery.** `git grep 3164 -- packages/core/src` returns exactly one hit, a content-contract test over skill text. The doctrine's stated escape hatch — "deliberate gate changes need issue/PR rationale (constitution-tier disposal under #3164)" — is prose pointing at prose. Remedy 2 would be the **first** mechanization of #3164, a materially bigger lift than "make the doctrine's own escape hatch mechanical" implies, and it should be scoped as such.
- **The clearance token is agent-authored untrusted text.** Remedy 2 accepts "an issue or PR link in the commit body." The party writing that token is the party being evaluated, and `Refs #1` satisfies it. `--allow-coverage-debt=#N` (#2573) already has that shape and that weakness. A detector that treats any well-formed reference as clearance converts a hard rule into a typing exercise; the token must resolve to an issue whose body names the gate change as the change, or it buys nothing.
- **Shared-dest concurrency.** Any base-ref differ must resolve its base from the recorded dispatch/base SHA, not from `HEAD~1` or a moving branch ref. Multiple seats in one dest (this arc's own posture) each produce a locally-clean diff; a working-tree-only differ sees nothing. `verify:scope-provenance` already takes `--base-ref` explicitly — reuse that convention.
- **Two chokepoints is a day-one bypass.** Per finding 3, a detector wired only into `gatesForCheckTarget` is invisible to `task deft:check`, and one wired only into the Taskfile is invisible to `deft check`. It must land in both, and `verify:consumer-check-contract` must be taught to fail on divergence, or the gate ships with a documented bypass.

## Road not taken, and what would flip this

There was a real fork: **extend #3322's red -> method-change -> green pairing to gate lanes**, versus **a fresh base-ref differ over evaluator-surface paths**. I argue for pairing (finding 1), because it is the only one of the two that can separate the correct gate edit from the self-serving one — the issue's own central observation is that the diffs are identical, and only the preceding observed red distinguishes them.

Steelmanning the differ, the stronger rejected position: it needs no telemetry substrate, so it is immune to finding 2 entirely; it works on a cold CI clone with no session history; and it catches the case pairing structurally cannot — an agent that lowers a floor **pre-emptively**, before ever running the lane red, so no `fail` event exists to pair against. That case is real, and the issue's framing ("the cheapest path to green") makes it likely.

What would flip my verdict: if the coverage lane cannot be made to emit a `verification` event carrying a `method_fingerprint` over the measurement scope — i.e. if `commandCountFromFingerprint`'s `cmd\0cmd\0cwd-or-hash` encoding cannot represent "which packages were measured" — then pairing has no signal for this surface and the differ is the only option. That is a small, concrete, checkable question, and the lean should answer it before binding remedy 1 rather than after.
